Kevin (CS): heads up — BrightApps pinged us asking for a clear post-incident note after last night's latency spike. can we draft the brief and confirm timeline + whether to offer an SLA credit?
Sam - Eng: quick timeline from infra: 01:12 UTC alerts (increased tail latency), 01:17 mitigation deployed (connection pooling tweak + scale-up), 01:25 full recovery. root cause was an unexpected KV cache eviction cascade when a rolling kernel update changed memory pressure behavior.
Oncall Bot: paging history: alerted @sam-eng at 01:12, handoff to @alex_p at 02:00, incident acknowledged at 02:03.
Alex P: for the status page I think we should keep it short and concrete. suggested wording below. open to edits.
StatusPage Bot: suggested status snippet:

"We experienced elevated latency between 01:12 UTC and 01:25 UTC due to an internal cache eviction regression during routine maintenance. Traffic was routed and autoscaling engaged; we completed mitigation and returned to normal service at 01:25 UTC. We are investigating root cause and will publish an RCA with preventative actions."

Kevin (CS): that reads fine. customer asked for a timeline with what we changed and what we are doing to prevent recurrences. Sylvia — can you draft the RCA summary for customer-facing language? keep it non-technical but accurate.
Sylvia S: draft below — please review and simplify if needed for BrightApps legal/comms.

```
RCA summary for BrightApps — (customer-facing):

What happened:
On 2026-02-18 at ~01:12 UTC our serving infrastructure experienced an increase in request latency affecting a subset of requests for approximately 13 minutes. The root cause was a cache eviction interaction triggered by a routine kernel and maintenance update that changed memory behavior on a small set of hosts.

What we did to fix it:
- We rolled a targeted mitigation (connection pooling and temporary eviction policy adjustment) and increased capacity to affected hosts. These actions restored normal latency by 01:25 UTC.

Preventative actions:
- Revert the problematic kernel parameter change on hosts in the affected pool and add a pre-deploy memory-pressure check.
- Add an automated KV cache health probe and alerting so we detect eviction cascades before customer impact.
- Update our maintenance runbook to include a canary window and stricter rollout controls for kernel-level changes.

Customer impact and compensation:
- You may have seen increased latency for a subset of requests between 01:12–01:25 UTC. We can offer a one-time pro-rated SLA credit for that window. Please let us know if you prefer a credit or a complimentary support session to review your request patterns.
```

Kevin (CS): LGTM. Maria / Jamal — are we ok to offer a pro-rated credit as standard? what does policy say for 13-minute blips?
Maria G: policy: credits are offered when a customer experiences measurable SLA breach. this looks borderline but BrightApps is on an enterprise plan so propose offering a gesture credit and a follow-up call. documented precedent: we usually provide a pro-rated credit for >10m impact when it affects percent of requests >0.5%. need ops to confirm percent affected.
Jamal R: ops numbers: ~1.2% of total requests for BrightApps hit higher latency distribution; user-facing error rate remained negligible. so threshold crossed.
Kevin (CS): ok offer a pro-rated credit + 30-min technical review with their platform team. I'll draft the customer email — please sign off.
Sylvia S: customer email draft below. please annotate changes inline.

```
Hi <BrightApps Contact>,

Thanks for raising this. We observed elevated request latency impacting a small portion of your traffic between 01:12–01:25 UTC on 2026-02-18. Our engineers identified a cache eviction cascade triggered by a recent kernel-level change during routine maintenance, and we applied a targeted mitigation and capacity increase which restored normal performance at 01:25 UTC.

What we’re doing next:
- Reverted the kernel change for the affected host pool and added a pre-deploy memory-pressure check.
- Implementing an automated cache-health probe and tighter canary controls for future maintenance.

As a courtesy for the impact you experienced, we will issue a pro-rated SLA credit for the affected window and would like to schedule a 30-minute technical review to walk through the incident and your request patterns. Please let us know your preferred time.

Apologies for the disruption — we know even short incidents are disruptive and we’re taking steps to prevent recurrence.

Best,
Kevin (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
```

Alex P: tiny wording nit — change "kernel-level change" to "kernel parameter update" to avoid sounding alarming. also prefer "we reverted the parameter change" instead of "reverted the kernel change".
Kevin (CS): updated.

Sylvia S: will push final RCA doc to the customer-facing doc repo after we get signoff here. also adding the internal postmortem link: https://redwood.internal/pm/INC-2211 (placeholder)
Oncall Bot: incident handoff note — oncall transfer completed at 02:00 UTC from @sam-eng to @alex_p.
PagerDuty: log: incident INC-2211 closed by @sam-eng at 02:30 UTC after post-incident checks.
Kevin (CS): next steps: 1) Ops to confirm percent affected in export (Jamal) 2) Legal/Comms to approve wording (Maria) 3) Final email + status page post scheduled once approved (Alex/Sylvia). Target to send customer note within 6 business hours.
Maria G: approved wording for customer email and status page. credits team — please prepare a pro-rated credit for 13 minutes for BrightApps, mark for enterprise gesture.
Jamal R: ops numbers exported and attached to incident (internal). confirmed 1.2% of requests hit elevated latency.
Kevin (CS): thanks all. I'll queue the status page update and send the customer email after credit confirmation. tagging this thread for any late edits. :thumbsup:
Alex P: I'll also prepare a short internal comms blurb for the product team.
Sylvia S: final note — adding the preventative work into the upcoming maintenance checklist and tracking as action item A-2211.
Kevin (CS): ok wrapping up. if no objections by 10:30 UTC I'll publish the status page update and send the customer note.
Maria G: no objections.
Kevin (CS): publishing and sending now.
StatusPage Bot: published update at 10:45 UTC: "Investigating (resolved) — Elevated latency 01:12–01:25 UTC. RCA and remediation actions forthcoming."
Kevin (CS): thread closed after customer confirmation call scheduled for tomorrow. thanks everyone.
